title: RDP connection-graph summary: expected star pattern vs. anomalous peer-to-peer pattern
event_type: Connection-graph / NDR session-aggregation result, one representative row per source host over a 24-hour window, port 3389

fields.label: HostRole (baseline)
fields.value: Standard workstation, not a jump host

fields.label: ExpectedPattern (segment baseline)
fields.value: 2 designated jump hosts each connect outbound to many workstations; workstations do not connect to each other

callouts.explanation: A workstation initiating RDP to nine other workstations is the anomalous peer-to-peer shape the section contrasts with the expected star pattern, where only jump hosts fan out to many targets.
None of the nine destinations are servers or the segment's designated jump hosts, which is what makes this off-baseline direction rather than ordinary administrative RDP traffic.
Stating the segment's normal 'few jump hosts, many targets' star topology alongside the observed row is what lets an analyst recognize the deviation without needing the full graph rendered.
A subset of sessions negotiating down to a weaker security layer than the environment's baseline expects is the pre-encryption anomaly signal described alongside session fan-out in this section.

note: Illustrative and conceptual only, representing one row an underlying connection-graph visualization would be built from; not a rendered graph, captured NDR screenshot, or product interface.
